text:
Alex Chen: quick heads-up — ran `npm audit` against console/ui (main) after the CI upgrade and saw 2 HIGH + 3 MODERATE advisories that affect the runtime bundle. attaching the audit snippet and initial triage notes.

Marta Rodriguez: can you paste the vulnerable package chain? I can pick this up for triage.

Alex Chen: yeah — top hit is CVE-2024-xxxx (serialize-javascript) pulled in via html-minifier-terser -> terser -> webpack. also a devtoolchain advisory in source-map-support that's flagged high for some transitive paths. full audit: `npm audit --json` gave:
```
# high: serialize-javascript via html-minifier-terser > terser > webpack
# high: source-map-support (transitive in build/test scripts)
# moderate: left-padish dep in some legacy demo package
```

Liam Patel: ok. Repro steps: `npm ci && npm run build:prod` then observe terser warnings. Likely fix is to bump terser or replace html-minifier-terser; webpack 5.72 -> 5.75 picked up newer terser in some scenarios. Lockfile churn will happen if we upgrade webpack or regenerate package-lock.

Sasha Ivanov: priority wise — this is public-facing console code. I'd treat serialize-javascript as HIGH RISK for XSS-like transformations if exploited. Recommend hotfix-level prioritization. Can we do a minimal patch (upgrade terser/html-minifier-terser) without touching app deps?

Alex Chen: trying `npm update terser --depth 5` in a local branch produced partial resolution but left html-minifier-terser pinned. `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` reduced the count but CI still flags one high. If we can't resolve transitively, plan B = update html-minifier-terser or switch to html-minifier with maintained fork.

Marta Rodriguez: propose workflow: 1) reproduce + minimal fix on hotfix branch 2) run full CI/e2e 3) canary deploy 10% 4) monitor errors & security logs 5) backport to release branch. I'll own the Jira: SEC-412.

deploy-bot: created jira SEC-412 and opened PR #789 (branch: hotfix/console-terser-patch). CI triggered.

sec-bot: recommended actions: fail CI on HIGH advisories, auto-notify sec-oncall, and schedule immediate canary for public clusters. Severity matrix suggests <24h TTR for high on public UI.

Liam Patel: PR #789 notes: updated package.json devDeps: html-minifier-terser@^6.0.0 -> 7.0.1, terser@^5.18.0 -> 5.20.3. Command run:
```
# generate lockfile only, minimize churn
npm audit fix --package-lock-only || pnpm install --lockfile-only
```
Lockfile diff is ~150 lines, mostly devDeps. Bundled artifact checks (sha + smoke tests) passing locally.

Sasha Ivanov: before merging: add a small integration test that asserts `bundle-size` + basic DOM sanity for the console HTML output. Also add a rollback plan in PR description.

Alex Chen: agree. Also let's avoid unnecessary runtime dep bumps. If lockfile churn touches other transitive runtime libs, call it out in the PR body and include a one-line rationale for each changed top-level dep.

Marta Rodriguez: CI change: I'll add `scripts/security-audit.sh` that runs `npm audit --json` and fails the job if any high advisory is present. We'll gate it to exclude docs-only branches.

Liam Patel: opened PR with the changes, added test, linked SEC-412. ETA for review + canary deploy ~ 90m.

Sasha Ivanov: deployment checklist:
- merge hotfix PR
- wait for canary pipeline (10%)
- monitor Sentry & audit logs for 2h
- if anything: revert PR commit + purge CDN cache + redeploy previous image

Alex Chen: perfect. tagging @Marta Rodriguez as sec-oncall for the window. /cc @Liam Patel for release coordination. :thumbsup:
